subject.title: Feature Request: Add channel creation to message tool

question: What authorization and credential model should govern agent-created Slack and Discord channels?
rationale: Channel creation is an administrative workspace or server mutation rather than ordinary message delivery, so automation cannot safely choose requester authority, executing credentials, or whether agent and operator CLI authority should differ.

options.title: Explicit provider gates
options.body: Require default-off provider action gates, trusted-requester checks, and least-privilege credentials before advertising or executing channel creation.

options.title: Operator CLI only
options.body: Expose channel creation only through an operator-run CLI while keeping it unavailable to agent message-tool calls.

options.title: Keep external
options.body: Leave channel provisioning to direct Slack and Discord administration APIs outside OpenClaw.

recommendation.title: Explicit provider gates
recommendation.body: Require default-off provider action gates, trusted-requester checks, and least-privilege credentials before advertising or executing channel creation.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior detailed review covers the exact authority question and the relevant current surfaces.
